Music

Shining Bright

Singer-songwriter Erin Lunsford sparkles with new album “Rhinestones,” while keeping her roots alive.

Andrew Cothern
Andrew Cothern
Jul 22, 2026
Share
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
Copy URL
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 4:41
    Instaread

    If there’s one word to sum up singer-songwriter Erin Lunsford’s new sophomore solo album, it’s gratitude.

    “This album is kind of a snapshot of life in my early 30s,” she says of these folk and Americana songs. “There’s love and loss, family dynamics, career highs and lows. But the throughline of it all is finding gratitude in what you have despite the frustrations.”

    With her new album, “Rhinestones,” the Fincastle, Virginia native and Style Weekly Top 40 Under 40 recipient explores her dreams, as well as the rejections and resilience of her music career.

    “It’s kind of a way to honor my Appalachian roots and keep this part of my creative self alive,” she says, adding that she was inspired by her bluegrass and folk upbringing, but also draws inspiration from artists like Eva Cassidy, Brandi Carlile and Dan Tyminski alongside soundtracks from films such as “O Brother Where Art Thou?” and “Cold Mountain.”

     

    Singles for this record, which was produced by Lunsford and Jacob Ungerleider and recorded at Spacebomb Studios, have had a steady release schedule all year. Lunsford has seen many people at her shows identify with songs like “Watch Out For Deer,” about leaving town and saying goodbye to family, or “Crossing Belvidere,” where she shares a humorous story about her car breaking down on the Belvidere Bridge.

    “The singles approach was kind of cool because I got to tell so much of the story for each song and people were really connecting with them,” she says. “They were telling me their stories and are like, ‘My family says that phrase too’ or ‘I also broke down on the way to a gig.’ I love hearing how people relate to these songs. My ideal scenario is somebody putting one of my songs in a movie and having it live in other people’s art, so even more people can hear it, and it to have a life of its own.”

     

    Lunsford started her full band Erin and the Wildfire in 2011 when she moved to Central Virginia, but found that the band’s musical identity quickly began leaning more towards funk and indie pop, leaving her Americana tendencies to herself. While working on music with the Wildfire, she was building a catalog of her own music in her compartmentalized music brain.

    “Sometimes when I come up with a song, it’s so clear which bucket it needs to go in in terms of genre,” Lunsford says, adding that the Wildfire as a group isn’t going anywhere, but slowing down a bit while she focuses on her solo endeavors. “‘Name So Pretty,’ for example, was one song that could have been a Wildfire song. But we ended up keeping some acoustic elements that fit better with my folk style. It’s fun to figure out where the song is best served. Is it with my Americana stuff or is it more of an indie pop Wildfire situation?”

    She adds that sometimes she writes song that don’t fit either of those genres, so she needs a third project, “like a punk project,” she says, laughing.

    Lunsford has also taken unconventional approaches to promoting her new songs, including becoming a social media content creator, something she says was out of her wheelhouse but she had amazing collaborators who were able to build on her ideas. One such project was setting up a working telephone hotline to promote her song “Call Me If You Need Me” with multiple prompts for callers needing her words of encouragement or offers to haunt their exes.

    “I always want to think about what’s serving the music the best,” she says. “Like what’s going to allow it to be the best version it can be. Sometimes that’s letting go of my ego and allowing the song to live in a different place than I planned.”

     

    Through this album, Lunsford also sees her own resilience that she found her career path as a full-time musician.

    “That’s why the title track is ‘Rhinestones,’” she says. “It looks pretty, but it’s also a lot of work. These songs go into wanting to grow my career, but I don’t want to get stuck focusing on any setbacks. I’m balancing that feeling with the appreciation I have for the community that I do have. I don’t take it for granted at all. I just love making music.”

    Erin Lunsford will be celebrating the release of “Rhinestones” with a pop-up performance at Plan 9 Music on Thursday, July 23 at 6:30 p.m. ahead of her album release shows at Potter’s Craft Cider in Charlottesville on July 30 and The Camel on Friday, July 31. For more on Lunsford, visit erinlunsford.com.
